text:
maria: Heads up — after flipping FP8 on rtx-pool for webgen-3b canary we see a reproducible quality dip on our regression eval (~1.8% deg_score delta, n=1k prompts). Not huge but persistent.
ash: Oof. Is it across all prompt classes or a slice? link to run? :eyes:
maria: Mostly long-chain-of-thought / code-gen prompts. Short chat prompts look fine. Uploading two failing examples below.
---
jordan: paste samples please, easier to triage
maria: ```
PROMPT: "Implement a function to merge k sorted lists"
BASE (int8): returns canonical merge using heapq, complexity notes ok
FP8: returns workable code but drops an edge-case comparator and adds a wrong off-by-one
METRICS: base exact-match 0.78, fp8 0.62
```
ash: thanks. That smells like numeric instability in attention/FFN for larger context.
sasha: can we quickly bisect which layers are introducing the regression? we have the per-layer override hook in runtime now
eli: I can run a bisect across the FFN layers + attention projection layers. quick plan:
```bash
# run hybrid: fall back specific layers to int8
python infra/quant_bisect.py --model webgen-3b --profile fp8 --slice "layers=0-24" --target-slice-size 3 --metric deg_score
```
```bash
deploy-bot: Canary toggle applied: webgen-3b fp8 -> hybrid-int8 on layers 10-16 for canary (id: cb-452)
```
ash: great. Run with n=200 per slice for faster signal.
maria: running now, posting outputs in ~20m
--- 18m later ---
eli: quick results from bisect (n=200 each):
- layers 0-8: delta ~ -0.2% (insignificant)
- layers 9-12: delta ~ -1.4%
- layers 13-16: delta ~ -1.6%
- layers 17-24: delta ~ -0.1%
jordan: that narrows it to ~9-16 (attention + early FFNs)
sasha: hypothesis: FP8 quant noise in attention projection matrices causing token-prob distribution shift during long reasoning chains
ash: could also be kv-cache accumulation sensitivity — FP8 rounding might bias cached keys/values over long contexts
maria: can we confirm by doing per-layer AB: switch those layers to INT8/FP8 and run the failing sample set (n=1k) and collect token-prob delta
eli: yes. I'll run two ablation points: (A) layers 9-12 INT8, rest FP8; (B) layers 13-16 INT8, rest FP8; (C) both groups INT8.
qa-bot: starting eval job eva-879, dataset=long-reasoning-1k, metrics=(deg_score, token_prob_skew), timeout=2h
--- later ---
eli: results: (full 1k)
A: deg_score delta -0.9% (improved from -1.8)
B: deg_score delta -1.0%
C: deg_score delta -0.4%  <-- best
token_prob_skew: reduced by ~15% in C vs pure FP8
maria: so combined fallback on 9-16 to INT8 removes most regression. Good signal.
ash: ops question: performance/cost hit for forcing INT8 on those layers? we need numbers
eli: perf: tail latency +7%, tokens/sec -9% on rtx-pool for hybrid C. cost delta ~ +12% per-token CPU/GPU cycles for that model in current config.
jordan: tradeoff seems acceptable as temporary safety net while we probe quant kernels
sasha: next steps:
- open issue to investigate kernel-level precision mismatch on attention matmul (assign to eng-runtime)
- add optional profile that pins layers 9-16 to int8 for webgen-3b in production until fixed
- add unit/regression tests for long-ctx chain-of-thought prompts in the quant CI
maria: I'll file the canary rollback policy: if deg_score > 1.0% on weekly eval we auto-fallback to hybrid profile.
ash: extra: can we try FP8 with a small per-layer scale calibration tweak? maybe per-channel clipping tighter on proj weights
eli: I'll run a calibration sweep: two params --clip-pct and --calib-samples. will run grid and post.
deploy-bot: Canary cb-452 updated -> hybrid-profile applied to canary group (20% traffic)
qa-bot: eva-880 created: calibration-sweep-24jobs
maria: thanks team. Good triage flow. Keep logs/results in issue #4276 and we can discuss kernel changes in runtime sync tomorrow.
ash: :thumbsup:
